Sheet.Name: Name
Sheet.HpFollows: Max HP follows {base} + Toughness until the first Long Rest or Improving.
Sheet.RolledHint: The score you rolled. Your class's +1, lost Sanity and temporary changes (− and + below) are added on top.
Sheet.BoostedHint: The total in use. Click to change the number underneath ({base}); the bonuses below are added on top.
Sheet.AddTooltip: Create a new one here and open it
Sheet.LowerSanity: Lose 1 Sanity for a while. Rest or a Triumph on a Panic test gives it back.
Sheet.RaiseSanity: Give back 1 lost Sanity; with none lost, a temporary +1
Sheet.ConditionStripHint: Active conditions. Click to open the Conditions tab.
Sheet.ActionsHint: What this character can do: equipped or loose items with a button, powers, spells and feats with a Use button. Items packed in a container or dropped are not listed.
Sheet.NoActions: Nothing to use yet. Carry or equip an item, or add a power, spell or usable feat.

Equipment.DropHint: Drag weapons, armour, shields, gear, containers, scrolls and relics from the Items sidebar onto this sheet. A spell dropped here becomes a scroll of that spell.

Equipment.WornAsHint: Where this item is worn. Items with the same tag cannot be worn together (two cloaks, or shoes and boots). Items worn anywhere, such as rings and necklaces, never get in the way. Anything can also be held in a hand.
Equipment.NothingFits: Nothing you carry fits here. Set an item's "Worn as" on its sheet.
Equipment.CarriedHint: Drag an item onto a slot, or click a slot to choose.
Equipment.DoesNotFit: {name} cannot go there. Check its "Worn as" on its sheet.
Equipment.TakenOff: {names} taken off to make room for {name}.
Equipment.VersatileHint: This weapon is versatile: in one hand its attacks are +2 DR; in both hands, the other hand is taken.
Equipment.PutOn: Put on (its own slot, or a free hand)
Equipment.PlacedHint: Worn or held. Change it on the Equipment tab.
Equipment.ChooseFigure: Choose a picture to show instead of the skeleton

Item.MedicineHint: Ticked for a medicine box: it gets a Use button on the character sheet that heals d6 HP, cures Infected or ends persistent bleeding.
Item.QuantityHint: How many you carry, such as 6 torches or 10 iron nails. Each one counts towards cumbersome items and container space. Lower it by hand when you use one up; lights do it themselves when lit.
Item.CumbersomeHint: Counts towards your cumbersome limit: things too unwieldy to carry with ease, such as a two-handed weapon, a heavy shield, armour you are not wearing, a barrel or a body. The Dark Master decides what is cumbersome. Armour you are wearing never counts.

Weapon.ZeroHint: Leave a number at 0 if the weapon does not have that trait.
Weapon.AttackAbilityHint: The ability every attack with this weapon tests, instead of the usual one (the Spirit-linked sword: Presence).

Trait.agileHint: The Bane for attacking more than once in a turn starts only after your second attack.
Trait.finesseHint: Choose whether to attack with Agility or Strength.
Trait.versatileHint: Can be used one-handed, but attacks are +2 DR.
Trait.reachHint: Melee reach in feet instead of 5′.
Trait.thrownHint: Can be thrown without Bane up to this many feet. It must be retrieved before it is used again.
Trait.rangedHint: Bane when firing at something farther away than this many feet.
Trait.expendableHint: Roll this die after use (for ammunition, after a combat in which it was used). On a 1 it is used up.

Armour.MetalHint: Metal armour of tier 2 or heavier gives Bane on spellcasting. Tier 2 and up starts as metal; untick it for hide, leather and other non-metal armour.
Armour.TierHint: Damage lowers the current tier. Repairs can never raise it above the original tier.

Shield.Hint: Use an action to gain light (−2 DR to defend) or heavy (−4 DR) cover until the start of your next turn. An attack that only the cover stopped strikes the shield: a heavy shield becomes light, a light one is destroyed.
Shield.DestroyedHint: Struck while giving light cover. A destroyed shield gives no cover. Untick it once the shield is replaced.

Test.BoonBaneHint: Boon: roll two d20, keep the higher. Bane: keep the lower. Both together cancel out.
Test.AidHint: +1 for each ally who succeeded, −1 for each who failed; ±2 at most.
Test.ArmourDialogNote: {name}: {armour} DR on Agility tests, added for you.
Test.EncumberedBane: Encumbered: Bane on Strength and Agility tests.

Fortune.NoCharacter: You need a character of your own to burn Fortune on this card.
Fortune.NoGM: The Dark Master must be online to change this card.
Fortune.Gone: This card can no longer be changed: its character is gone.
Fortune.NotNow: That Fortune use is no longer offered on this card.
Fortune.DialogHint: Burn 1 Fortune for each, paid when you roll.
Fortune.ShieldBack: {name} is whole again and still raised.

Contest.Tooltip: Roll against an opponent: the higher total wins
Contest.FoeHint: A foe rolls a plain d20 and adds nothing. Its name is only used on the card.
Contest.CharacterHint: The opponent's ability, Boon and Bane count only when the opponent is a character.
Contest.Tie: A tie: no victor, the struggle goes on

Chance.SplitNote: {item}: no Neutral result. {split} or more is the best possible outcome, less the worst.

Expendable.Tooltip: Roll the expendable die ({die}): on a 1 it is used up
Expendable.UsedUpHint: Ticked when the expendable die rolls a 1 on the last one. Untick it if the item is refilled.
Expendable.OutOfAmmoHint: Ticked when the expendable die rolls a 1. The weapon cannot be reloaded until you untick it, for example after buying a new supply of ammunition.

Reload.LoadedHint: A weapon with Reload must be reloaded after each shot.
Reload.FireTooltip: Fire: the weapon is empty until reloaded
Reload.ActionsSpent: Spend {count} Interact actions to reload. The weapon is loaded.
Reload.ActionsUsed: Used {count} Interact actions to reload. The weapon is loaded.
Reload.NotYourTurn: Reloading uses actions, so in combat you can only do it on your own turn.
Reload.NoActions: Reloading needs {count} actions and you have fewer left this turn. Reloading anyway; the Dark Master decides.

Ammunition.Explanation: Ammunition was used in this combat. Roll its expendable die: on a 1 you have run out of ammunition.

Random.ChooseTooltip: Choose ancestry and class, roll the rest
Random.ChooseHint: Choose the ancestry and class. Everything else is rolled as for a random character: abilities, name, ancestry feat, background, spell, starting equipment and details.
Random.Replace: Roll a fully new character? Everything on {name}'s sheet is wiped: every item, feat, power and spell, abilities, HP, wounds, silver, Fortune, conditions, Details and notes, the name, and the minions that serve {name}. A new name is rolled. Only the portrait and token image stay. This cannot be undone.
Random.FortuneLine: The old character is wiped. Starting Fortune (d3): {fortune}.
Random.MinionKept: {minion} still serves this character: only its owner or the Dark Master can let it go.
Random.NoAncestryFeat: No ancestry feat found for this ancestry.
Random.NoneFound: No {type} found in the world or the compendiums.

Personality.RollTooltip: Roll on the table (rules 2.7). Replaces what is written here.
Personality.TableMissing: The personality table was not found in the Roll Tables compendium.

DialogueStage.Name: In-character dialogue box
DialogueStage.Hint: Show in-character chat and emotes at the bottom of the screen, visual novel style, with the speaker's art. Click the box to finish a line or dismiss it. Only on your own screen.

SplashesForAll.Name: Triumph and Ruin splashes
SplashesForAll.Hint: When a roll shows a Triumph or a Ruin, a banner with the roller's art and the result sweeps across every player's screen. Untick to switch it off for everyone.

TriumphSplash.Name: Show Triumph and Ruin splashes on my screen
TriumphSplash.Hint: Untick to hide the Triumph and Ruin splashes on your own screen only. Other players still see them.

MovementAnimations.Name: Movement animations
MovementAnimations.Hint: Tokens hop when they walk, lift off when they fly, sway when they swim, and so on. Off by default if your computer asks for reduced motion.

ShowHoverDistance.Name: Show distance on hover
ShowHoverDistance.Hint: When you hover over a token, show how far it is from your selected token (or, with none selected, from the token whose turn it is), counted edge to edge.

ShowReach.Name: Show reach while dragging
ShowReach.Hint: In combat, on a token's own turn, shade every square it can still reach this turn while you drag it, coloured by the Move action that pays for it.

CreationHelper.Name: Creation Helper
CreationHelper.Hint: Characters are made at random by default. Switch this on to show the Creation Helper button on character sheets, for choosing each step by hand, and to let players choose their feat when Improving.

UseWeather.Name: Use the Weather subsystem
UseWeather.Hint: Weather is an optional subsystem. Switch this off and no weather is rolled at a new day or while travelling, the Calendar panel shows no weather, and weather hazards have no effect. Today's weather is kept for when you switch it back on.

PlayersImprove.Name: Players can improve
PlayersImprove.Hint: Show the Improve button to players on their own characters, not only to the Dark Master. The Dark Master still decides when a character improves.

ImprovingGroup.Name: Improving feat group
ImprovingGroup.Hint: When improving, either roll a d3 for a general, ancestry or class feat, or let whoever improves choose the group. The feat within the group is still rolled.

UiMood.Name: Interface mood
UiMood.Hint: VÅR BORG windows, chat cards and orbs look hopeful in light and threatening in darkness. Follow my character: they change when your character's token is In Darkness. Always light or Always dark keeps one look, for comfort or legibility. Only on your own screen.

Examples.Label: Import examples
Examples.Hint: Create the example documents used to test the system, or reset them to their saved values if they are already in this world.
Examples.Title: Import examples
Examples.Explanation: This creates every example in the world. Examples that are already here are updated to their saved values, so any changes you made to them are lost.
Examples.GMOnly: Only the GM can import examples.
Examples.Failed: The examples could not be imported. Press F12 and look in the console for details.

Container.Hint: A container lets you find what you need. It does not raise your cumbersome limit.

Movement.EditSpeeds: Speeds: extra walking feet, and fly, swim and climb
Movement.DialogHint: Feet per Move action. Leave a box blank if the character cannot move that way.

Hint.walkBonus: Added to the walking speed from carrying (20′). Can be negative. Overloaded still means 0.
Hint.other: Feet per Move. Overloaded makes it 0.

Movement.DiagonalsWarning: VÅR BORG counts every second diagonal step double. Set Game Settings → Core → Grid Diagonals to "Alternating (1/2)" for the ruler to match the rules.
Movement.NotEnough: {name} cannot move that far: it costs {cost} and {left} is left this turn.
Movement.LeftHint: {feet}′ left from the last Move. Lost when an action is spent on anything else.
Movement.CreatureHint: Feet per Move action. Leave fly, swim or climb blank if it cannot move that way.

Hint.normal: You can carry cumbersome items up to your Toughness (minimum 1). Other items do not count.
Hint.encumbered: Encumbered: all terrain counts as difficult terrain, and Bane on Strength and Agility tests.
Hint.overloaded: More than twice your cumbersome limit: your movement is 0. You are also Encumbered: Bane on Strength and Agility tests.

Feat.ImprovingHint: Tick this if the feat was chosen when Improving. Only these feats raise the DR of the Death’s Door Sanity test.

BelongsTo.Hint: The name of the ancestry or class this belongs to. The creation helper offers it only for that ancestry or class.

Foe.MoraleHint: Roll 2d6: above its Morale, the foe is demoralised. A foe with Morale – never rolls.
Foe.ArmourHint: Subtracted from damage that hits the foe.
Foe.InitiativeHint: Added to the foe’s d6 initiative roll. It comes from the foe’s passives, so type it in when a passive grants one.
Foe.MookHint: A mook has 1 HP, fails every test and never rolls Morale. It keeps its attacks and passives but has no gloom abilities.
Foe.DropHint: Drag weapons (attacks) and feats (passives) from the Items sidebar onto this sheet, or use the Add buttons.
Foe.AttackHint: A foe’s attack: melee or ranged, its damage, and its reach or range. Foe attacks have no other traits and no expendable die.
Foe.RangeHint: How far the ranged attack reaches, such as 60 for (60′).
Foe.ReachHint: Melee reach in feet, such as 10 for (reach 10′). Leave at 0 for the usual 5′.

Combat.PipsLeft: {label}: {left} of {max} left. Click a filled pip to spend it, an empty one to give it back.

Strip.Tooltip: {name} (initiative {initiative}). Click to find them on the map.

Pools.Title: Ember and Gloom
Pools.Round: Round {round}: both pools filled to {fill}. Unspent charges are lost at the end of the round.
Pools.WeatherBonus: {hazard}: the {pool} pool gains an extra {symbol}{amount} this round.
Pools.WeatherBonusPanel: {hazard}: the {pool} pool gains an extra {symbol}{amount} each round.
Pools.OutsideCombat: Outside combat there is no pool.
Pools.NotEnough: The {pool} pool does not hold enough charges.
Pools.NoCombat: There is no pool outside combat.
Pools.GMOnly: Only the Dark Master can do that with the {pool} pool.
Pools.NoGM: The Dark Master must be connected to spend from the {pool} pool.
Pools.Bad: That is not a valid change to the {pool} pool.
Pools.Gained: {name} adds {symbol}{amount} to the {pool} pool with {source} ({left} now).

Orbs.Tooltip: {pool}: {left} left. Click to open the Ember and Gloom panel.

Day.Label: Day {day}
Day.NewDayTooltip: Start the next day and move the clock on to its dawn: Doomed characters gain a wound, those without food for more than 2 days take d6 damage, and those who did not sleep become Fatigued.
Day.AteHint: Ate and drank (yesterday) unticked: one more day without food. More than 2 days without food: d6 damage at the start of each day.
Day.SleptHint: Slept unticked: one more level of Fatigued. A Long Rest takes one away.
Day.NoCharacters: There are no living characters. Only the day number changes.
Day.DoomedWound: Doomed: gains a wound at the start of the day (wounds {wounds}/{max}).
Day.DoomedAtMax: Doomed: already at maximum wounds, so no wound is added.
Day.NextZeroDeathsDoor: {name} is at maximum wounds: the next 0 HP is Death's Door.
Day.WithoutFoodHint: Days in a row without food or drink. Set at each New day; more than 2 is starving (d6 damage at the start of each day).

Rest.Tooltip: Short rest, Long rest or Downtime for the characters.
Rest.KindHint: Short rest: full HP. Long rest: full HP, one wound, one Fatigued level, Fortune if at 0, and the next day begins. Downtime: heals everything except Doomed, Infected and lasting injuries, and 3 days pass. Every rest unlocks ember abilities.
Rest.AteHint: Ate and drank counts for a Long rest and Downtime only. Without it the rest gives no benefit.
Rest.InterruptedHint: Interrupted: the character tests Toughness DR{dr}. On a Failure the rest gives no benefit.
Rest.Cancelled: The rest was cancelled. Nothing has changed.
Rest.NoCharacters: No character can rest: they are dead or at Death's Door.
Rest.NobodyRests: Tick at least one character who rests.
Rest.HpFixed: First Long Rest: max HP is now fixed at {max}.
Rest.InfectedDamage: Takes {damage} damage at the end of the rest.

Attack.BeyondRangeHint: Tick if the target is farther away than {distance}. Bane.
Attack.AutomaticHint: Attacks are DR12. Heavy, one-handed, armour, Encumbered and conditions are added for you.
Attack.ArmourNote: {armour} DR for armour ({name}) on an Agility attack
Attack.MultipleNote: You have already attacked this turn: Bane.
Attack.MultipleNoteAgile: You have already attacked twice this turn: Bane, even with an agile weapon.
Attack.TurnNote: Your turn. Attacks made so far this turn: {count}. This attack uses an action.
Attack.ReactionNote: Not your turn: this attack uses your reaction and does not count towards the multiple-attack Bane.
Attack.NoTarget: No target. Target a token to name it on the card and lower its armour on a Triumph.
Attack.RetargetTooltip: Point this attack at the foe you target now. The roll stays the same.
Attack.RetargetNone: Target a foe first, then press the crosshairs to point the attack at it.
Attack.Retargeted: Retargeted at {name}. The roll and DR are unchanged.

Outcome.triumph: Double damage, and the foe’s armour is reduced by one tier.
Outcome.ruin: Your weapon jams or your grip falters: Bane on attacks until you spend an action to recover.

Attack.SeveralHint: Several targets: one attack roll and one damage roll count for all of them. Foes take it with Inflict damage (their armour soaks); characters and minions defend.
Attack.SeveralConditions: Several targets: the targets’ own conditions are not counted. Add Boon or Bane by hand if they matter.
Attack.ArmourToLower: Triumph: {name}’s armour should be lowered from {from} to {to} (the Dark Master can do it).
Attack.BadDamage: Damage “{formula}” is not a dice formula. Roll it by hand.
Attack.GMOnly: Only the Dark Master can change this foe.
Attack.Retrieve: A thrown weapon must be retrieved before it can be used again.
Attack.NoActions: No actions left this turn. The attack is rolled anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Attack.NoReaction: No reaction left. The attack is rolled anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Attack.RuinNote: Your last attack was a Ruin: Bane until you Recover.
Attack.RuinBane: Ruin not yet recovered from: Bane.
Attack.RuinedNow: Bane on your attacks until you press Recover on your sheet (one action).
Attack.RuinedHint: Bane on attacks until you Recover. In combat this uses one action (◈) on your turn.
Attack.Recovered: {name} recovers from the Ruin. Attacks no longer have Bane from it.
Attack.RecoverNotYourTurn: Recovering uses an action, so in combat you can only do it on your own turn.
Attack.RecoverNoActions: No actions left this turn. Recovering anyway; the Dark Master decides.

Defence.FoeAttackTooltip: Attack: post a card the target defends against
Defence.DefendHint: Foes do not roll. The target tests Agility to defend.
Defence.NoTargetHint: No character targeted. Whoever presses Defend defends with their own character.
Defence.AutomaticHint: Defence is Agility DR12. Heavy and special armour (+2 DR), a raised shield, Encumbered and conditions are added for you.

Outcome.triumph: You dodge, and can react with an Attack.
Outcome.ruin: You are hit: double damage, and your armour is reduced by one tier.

Defence.ZeroHp: 0 HP: see the wound card that follows.
Defence.ArmourDestroyed: {name}: tier {from} → {to}. Damaged below tier 1, it is destroyed.
Defence.ShieldDamaged: Only the cover stopped the blow: it strikes {name}, which is now a light shield.
Defence.ShieldDestroyed: Only the cover stopped the blow: it strikes {name}, which is destroyed.
Defence.RaiseTooltip: Raise shield: cover until the start of your next turn (◈)
Defence.Raised: {name} raises {shield}: {dr} DR to defend until the start of their next turn.
Defence.RaisedHint: {name}: −{dr} DR to defend until the start of your next turn.
Defence.RaiseNotYourTurn: Raising a shield uses an action, so in combat you can only do it on your own turn.
Defence.RaiseNoActions: No actions left this turn. Raising the shield anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Defence.NoCharacter: No character or minion to defend. Target one, select its token, or have a character assigned to you.

FoeDamage.Inflict: Inflict {damage} damage on the targeted foe
FoeDamage.NoFoe: No foe to damage. Target a foe’s token first.
FoeDamage.LastEnemy: {name} is the last enemy standing, with a third of its HP or less. It may roll Morale.
FoeDamage.HalfDown: Half the group is down. Each foe still standing may roll Morale.

MoraleRoll.Tooltip: Roll 2d6. Above its Morale the foe is demoralised: d6, 1–3 it flees, 4–6 it surrenders.
MoraleRoll.NeverTooltip: This foe never rolls Morale (Morale – or a mook).

Dice.high: 3d6, the two highest kept: likelier to break.
Dice.low: 3d6, the two lowest kept: likelier to hold.

Condition.Title: Conditions
Condition.FatigueHint: Levels of fatigue. 1 or more makes the character Fatigued; 0 ends it. There is no maximum.
Condition.TurnStart: {name} starts the turn with {actions} actions and {reactions} reactions ({conditions}).

Text.blinded: You can’t see. All terrain is difficult terrain. Bane on tests that rely on sight.
Text.deafened: You can’t hear. Bane on tests that rely on hearing.
Text.charmed: You are treated as a minion by the source of the charming. You cannot harm the charmer.
Text.fatigued: +2 DR on all tests for each level of fatigue. Reduced by one level upon a Long Rest.
Text.frightened: You’re deadly afraid of something. Bane on all tests targeting the source of your fear.
Text.stupefied: Your mind is slow and sluggish. Bane on tests that require thought, no reaction.
Text.restrained: You’re tied up, held, or pinned down. You can’t move. Bane on tests to defend and attack.
Text.prone: You’re flat on the ground. Move as if difficult terrain. Attack +2 DR. Defend against melee +2 DR, defend against ranged −2 DR.
Text.quickened: At the start of your next turn, you gain one additional action. Then it ends.
Text.silenced: You can’t speak. Some sources of silence may also suppress other sounds.
Text.slowed: At the start of your next turn, you gain one less action and one less reaction. Then it ends.
Text.deathsDoor: You are at 0 HP, unconscious, and near death. You cannot act. Roll on the Death’s Door table. You remain at Death’s Door for as long as you are unconscious.
Text.darkVessel: Gain d8 HP. Use all your actions to attack the nearest target by the most effective means. Attack −2 DR. Defend +2 DR. Ends when at Death’s Door, dead or otherwise incapacitated.
Text.infected: You gain no benefits from resting, take d6 damage at the end of a rest. Can be cured using a medicine box.
Text.doomed: You gain no benefits from resting, take 1 wound at the start of each day. You can be cured using special means.
Text.encumbered: All terrain counts as difficult terrain, and Bane on any Strength and Agility tests.
Text.persistentDamage: Take ongoing damage at the end of your turn. Each time you take persistent damage, test Toughness DR12 to overcome it; on a Success it ends. The Dark Master may adjust the DR.

FoeText.blinded: Foe: All terrain is difficult terrain. Attacks against it are made with Boon, and creatures defend against its attacks with Boon.
FoeText.deafened: Foe: It cannot hear. It does not notice sounds, and cannot be affected by or respond to anything it must hear.
FoeText.fatigued: Foe: For each level of fatigue, attacks against it are at −2 DR and creatures defend against it at −2 DR.
FoeText.frightened: Foe: Creatures defend with Boon against its attacks and gloom abilities that target the source of its fear.
FoeText.stupefied: Foe: No reaction. Creatures defend against its gloom abilities with Boon.
FoeText.restrained: Foe: It can’t move. Attacks against it are made with Boon, and creatures defend against its attacks with Boon.
FoeText.prone: Foe: Moves as if difficult terrain. Creatures defend against its attacks at −2 DR. Melee attacks against it are at −2 DR, ranged attacks against it at +2 DR.
FoeText.encumbered: Foe: All terrain is difficult terrain. Attacks against it are made with Boon, and creatures defend against its melee attacks with Boon.
FoeText.persistentDamage: Takes ongoing damage at the end of its turn. Each time it takes persistent damage, the Dark Master rolls a d20; on 12 or higher it ends.

test.blinded: Blinded: tick Bane if this test relies on sight.
test.deafened: Deafened: tick Bane if this test relies on hearing.
test.stupefied: Stupefied: tick Bane if this test requires thought.
test.frightened: Frightened: tick Bane if this test targets the source of your fear.
test.sprainedAnkle: Sprained ankle: tick Bane if this is a movement test.
test.concussion: Concussion: tick Bane if this is a mental test.
test.legBruised: Leg or foot bruised: tick Bane if this is a movement test.
test.armBruised: Arm or hand bruised: tick Bane if this is a manual task.

attack.blinded: Blinded: tick Bane if this attack relies on sight.
attack.frightened: Frightened: tick Bane if you are attacking the source of your fear.
attack.charmed: Charmed: you cannot harm the one who charmed you.

defence.blinded: Blinded: tick Bane if this defence relies on sight.
defence.deafened: Deafened: tick Bane if this defence relies on hearing.

foeAttack.frightened: Frightened: tick Boon if this attack targets the source of its fear.

Medicine.Tooltip: Use the medicine box (◈). Target a character to treat them, or none to treat yourself.
Medicine.DialogHint: Costs one action (◈). The box's expendable die is rolled either way. The patient tests Toughness DR{dr}; on a Success it works.
Medicine.OneTarget: Target only one character, or none to treat yourself.
Medicine.CharactersOnly: A medicine box can only treat a character.
Medicine.Dead: {name} is dead. A medicine box cannot help.
Medicine.NotYourTurn: In combat you can only use a medicine box on your own turn.
Medicine.NoActions: A medicine box needs one action and you have none left this turn. Using it anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Medicine.CardHint: The patient tests Toughness DR{dr}. On a Success it works.

Uses.FrequencyHint: How often it can be used. Once used, its Use button is off until it comes back: once per round at the start of each round and when combat ends, once per turn at the start of the character’s turn and when combat ends, once per encounter when combat ends, once per day at each new day, once per Long Rest at a Long Rest or Downtime, once per Downtime at Downtime, once per visit when the Dark Master presses Reset visit uses. New items take this from “once per …” in their text.
Uses.UsedHint: Used: its Use button is off until it comes back. Untick to give the use back by hand.
Uses.Tooltip: Use it ({frequency}). Posts its text to chat and marks it used.
Uses.UsedTooltip: Already used. It comes back on its own, or untick Used on the item.
Uses.InteractTooltip: Interact ◈: use it, then roll its expendable die ({die}). On a 1, one is used up.
Uses.ResetVisitTooltip: The party reaches a new settlement: every “once per visit” use (such as Haggler) comes back.
Uses.Which: What do you want to do?

Light.Label: Light
Light.Speaker: Light
Light.KindHint: A torch or candle burns itself when lit. A lantern burns one Lantern oil carried by the same character. Lit lights share one real-time timer on the Light panel.
Light.BurnsForHint: How long one lasts in real time, usually 60 minutes. For a lantern, set this on its oil.
Light.RangeHint: How far it lights, usually 30 feet (candle 10, torch 40, lantern 60). While the light timer runs, its character's tokens shine bright light this far, in the scene's units.
Light.Tooltip: Light it. With no light burning it starts the light timer; otherwise it joins the running timer. Uses one up.
Light.PausedHint: The game is paused: the light timer waits.
Light.BlackburnHint: Blackburn: lights burn twice as fast and shine half as far today.
Light.TorchTooltip: The light timer. Click to open the Light panel.
Light.TorchOutTooltip: No light burning. Click to open the Light panel.
Light.WeatherOrb: Weather: {weather}. Click to open the Calendar panel.
Light.PhaseOrb: {phase}, {clock} ({date}). Click to open the Calendar panel.
Light.StartTooltip: Start the light timer for this many minutes of real time.
Light.OutTooltip: Put the lights out now. No card is posted.
Light.Joins: It joins the running light timer: {clock} left.
Light.Waits: The game is paused: the timer waits until it goes on.
Light.Late: Lit in the last five minutes of the timer. The Dark Master may give it a new timer.
Light.NewTimerDone: The Dark Master gives the light a new timer: {clock}.
Light.OutText: The light timer has run out. Every light lit on it goes out, and the tokens it lit go dark.
Light.Darkness: Complete darkness gives Bane on all tests. For every hour spent in complete darkness, roll for a random encounter.
Light.NoFuel: {name} has no Lantern oil to burn in {item}.
Light.NoGM: The Dark Master must be connected to light a light.
Light.NotYours: You can only change the light of a character you own.
Light.StateDimmed: Your lantern is dimmed to 5 feet.
Light.DimTooltip: Dim the lantern so it sheds light to only 5 feet. It still burns on the light timer.
Light.TurnUpTooltip: Turn the lantern back up to its full range.
Light.PutOutTooltip: Put your light out. It is spent: lighting it again uses a new torch, candle or oil.
Light.PutOut: {name} puts out their light. It is spent.
Light.GMOnly: Only the Dark Master can change the light timer.
Light.Bad: That is not a valid number of minutes.
Light.Title: The Light

Persistent.Label: Persistent damage
Persistent.FormulaHint: Dice such as d4 or 2d4, or a number such as 7.
Persistent.TickHint: Deal all persistent damage now, as at the end of a turn. For use outside combat.
Persistent.Name: Persistent {type} damage ({formula})
Persistent.BadFormula: Persistent damage needs dice such as d4 or 2d4, or a number such as 7.
Persistent.WeakerRemoved: {name}: {removed} removed. Of the same type, only the strongest applies.
Persistent.Damage: {formula}: {damage} damage. Armour does not soak it.
Persistent.FoeGoesOn: Dark Master’s d20: {roll}. It goes on.
Persistent.MookFails: A mook fails every test: it goes on.
Persistent.AlreadyEnded: This persistent damage has already ended.
Persistent.RemoveHint: To remove persistent damage, use its ✕ in the Conditions section of the sheet.

Panic.Title: Panic
Panic.Tooltip: Panic test: Sanity DR12. On a Failure roll on the Panic table with 1d10, on a Ruin with 2d10. A Triumph restores lost Sanity.
Panic.CountsInCombat: In combat, one turn is used at the end of each of your turns (not the turn it was gained in). Outside combat, the Dark Master removes it.
Panic.NextTest: It counts for your next ability test, contest, attack or defence, and then ends.
Panic.SanityLost: Sanity {from} → {to}. Lost Sanity: {lost}. A Panic Triumph gives it back.
Panic.SanityAtMinimum: Sanity is already −3 and cannot go lower.
Panic.NewPhobia: Write the new phobia in Phobias on the character sheet.
Panic.NewPhobias: Write the two new phobias in Phobias on the character sheet.
Panic.TooDeep: Too many Compounding problems in a row: roll any more on the Panic table by hand.
Panic.ByHand: The system does not apply this. The Dark Master decides what happens to the character.

Group.Title: Group Panic test
Group.Speaker: Panic
Group.NoCharacters: No characters to test: select their tokens, or place them on the scene.

Panic.RuinAsFailure: {item}: {name}’s Ruin counts as a Failure, so the Panic table is rolled with 1d10.

Nerves.Offer: {item}: hold yourself together and treat the result as a Success, gaining one level of Fatigued, or roll on the Panic table.
Nerves.Spent: Steady nerves has already been used today.
Nerves.Held: {item}: {name} holds themselves together. The Panic test counts as a Success.
Nerves.Fatigued: The effort costs them: Fatigued, level {level}.

Panic.AddHint: Dark Master only. Gives the character a lasting Panic result, with its 1d10 duration rolled.
Panic.PhobiasHint: Test Panic whenever you encounter a phobia. A phobia is resolved on a Triumph on its Panic test.

terrified.name: Terrified
terrified.text: For 1d10 turns, you cannot willingly approach the source of your panic.

babbling.name: Babbling
babbling.text: For 1d10 turns, you babble incoherently. You cannot communicate.

distracted.name: Distracted
distracted.text: For 1d10 turns, your mind is occupied by terror. You do not gain a reaction at the start of your turn.

sluggish.name: Sluggish
sluggish.text: For 1d10 turns, your thoughts and movements are sluggish. At the start of your turn, you gain two actions instead of three.

screamingFit.name: Screaming Fit
screamingFit.text: For 1d10 turns, you scream in terror at the top of your lungs. Everyone can hear.

denial.name: Denial
denial.text: For 1d10 turns, you vehemently deny the existence of the source of your panic.

cripplingFear.name: Crippling Fear
cripplingFear.text: Gain a new permanent phobia. Test Panic whenever you encounter a phobia. A phobia is resolved on a Triumph on its Panic test.

fitOfViolence.name: Fit of Violence
fitOfViolence.text: For 1d10 turns, you lash out in violence. At the start of your turn, select a random target. You must attack this target by the most effective means.

descentIntoMadness.name: Descent into Madness
descentIntoMadness.text: You gain two new phobias. Test Panic whenever you encounter a phobia. A phobia is resolved on a Triumph on its Panic test.

flee.name: Flee
flee.text: For 1d10 turns, you must spend all your actions to get away as far as possible from the source of your panic.

faint.name: Faint
faint.text: You faint for 1d10 turns: no actions or reactions. Your allies can awaken you by spending three cumulative actions; then remove this.

cowardice.name: Cowardice
cowardice.text: For the next 1d10 hours, test Presence DR12 to engage in combat. Triumph: as Success, and you are no longer suffering from cowardice. Success: you engage in combat. Failure: you flee for one turn. Ruin: as Failure, and test Panic.

paranoid.name: Paranoid
paranoid.text: For the next 1d10 hours, whenever a character (re)joins your group, even after a short absence, test Presence DR12. Triumph: you are no longer paranoid. Success: you are put at ease. Failure: you consider this person fully untrustworthy. Ruin: as Failure, and you Panic whenever this person acts suspiciously.

compoundingProblems.name: Compounding Problems
compoundingProblems.text: Roll 2d10 twice on the Panic table.

psychologicalCollapse.name: Psychological Collapse
psychologicalCollapse.text: You become permanently and irreparably insane. You are effectively dead, and your character is taken over by the Dark Master.

Panic.EndsByClock: It ends by itself when that many hours have passed on the world clock.

Agony.Title: Table of Agony
Agony.HpReturns: HP returns to its maximum ({hp}). Any leftover damage is negated.
Agony.Purpose: Wound test: on a failure, roll on the Table of Agony. The Dark Master may change the DR.
Agony.ShrugsOff: {name} takes the wound without further harm.
Agony.Cracks: {name}'s body cracks: roll on the Table of Agony.
Agony.GmRolls: The Dark Master picks the column and rolls.
Agony.GmOnly: Only the Dark Master rolls on the Table of Agony.
Agony.TypeHint: The damage type of the weapon or persistent damage suggests a column. Choose the one that fits the source and severity of the harm.
Agony.NoSuggestion: Nothing suggests a column. Choose the one that fits the source and severity of the harm.
Agony.Persistent: Persistent {type} damage ({formula}) added. It deals damage at the end of your turn.
Agony.NextTest: It counts for your next ability test, contest, attack or defence, and then ends.
Agony.Lasting: A lasting injury, shown in Conditions. The Dark Master removes it when it heals or ends.
Agony.ReminderOnly: The system cannot judge which tests this covers: the test dialogue reminds you to tick Bane.
Agony.DeathsDoorInstead: {item}: {name} does not die, but goes to Death's Door instead.
Agony.Spared: {name} does not die (see the card above).
Agony.ByHand: The system does not apply this. The Dark Master decides what happens.

lotsOfBlood.name: Lots of blood
lotsOfBlood.text: Lots of blood. Those close by test Panic.

piercedSkin.name: Pierced skin
piercedSkin.text: Pierced skin, d4 persistent bleeding damage.

sprainedAnkle.name: Sprained ankle
sprainedAnkle.text: Sprained ankle, bane on movement tests.

bloodInEyes.name: Blood in eyes
bloodInEyes.text: Blood in eyes, bane until wiped clean.

hairBurnt.name: Hair burnt
hairBurnt.text: Hair burnt, bane on Presence tests.

legBruised.name: Leg or foot bruised
legBruised.text: Leg or foot bruised, bane on movement tests.

majorCut.name: Major cut
majorCut.text: Major cut, d4 persistent bleeding damage.

internalBleeding.name: Internal bleeding
internalBleeding.text: Internal bleeding, d4 persistent bleeding damage.

rippedFlesh.name: Ripped off flesh
rippedFlesh.text: Ripped off flesh, bane on Strength tests.

armBruised.name: Arm or hand bruised
armBruised.text: Arm or hand bruised, bane on manual tasks.

fingersSevered.name: Finger/toes severed
fingersSevered.text: Finger/toes severed, d6 persistent bleeding damage.

snappedCollarbone.name: Snapped collarbone
snappedCollarbone.text: Snapped collarbone, bane on Strength tests.

handSevered.name: Hand/foot severed
handSevered.text: Hand/foot severed, d6 persistent bleeding damage.

backBroken.name: Back broken
backBroken.text: Back broken, bane on all tests.

majorBloodLoss.name: Major blood loss
majorBloodLoss.text: Major blood loss, d8 persistent bleeding damage.

limbOnFire.name: Limb on fire
limbOnFire.text: Limb on fire, 1d10 persistent fire damage.

skullFracture.name: Skull fracture
skullFracture.text: Skull fracture, bane on all tests.

arteryCut.name: Major artery cut
arteryCut.text: Major artery cut, 2d6 persistent bleeding damage.

suckingChestWound.name: Sucking chest wound
suckingChestWound.text: Sucking chest wound, d8 persistent bleeding damage.

bodyOnFire.name: Body on fire
bodyOnFire.text: Body on fire, 2d10 persistent fire damage.

gutsSpooled.name: Guts spooled on floor
gutsSpooled.text: Guts spooled on floor, 7 persistent bleeding damage.

spineBroken.name: Spine or neck broken
spineBroken.text: Spine or neck broken, death's door.

throatSlit.name: Throat slit or heart pierced
throatSlit.text: Throat slit or heart pierced, death's door.

engulfed.name: Engulfed in fiery explosion
engulfed.text: Engulfed in fiery explosion, death's door.

Agony.ToDeathsDoor: Wounds go to their maximum and HP to 0: Death's Door.
Agony.HpUnchanged: HP does not change: blood spent on magic does not heal you.

DeathsDoor.Title: Death's Door
DeathsDoor.RollButton: Roll on the Death's Door table
DeathsDoor.ChooseHint: As the Dark Master you may choose the result instead of rolling, for example when a relic or feat lets the player roll twice.

darkPull.name: The dark pulls
darkPull.text: Sanity DR10, increased by 1 for each feat gained through Improving. Success: unconscious for d8 rounds, then awaken with 1 HP. Failure: Dark Vessel.

doomed.name: Doomed
doomed.text: Doomed, unconscious for d10 rounds, then awaken with 1 HP.

maimed.name: Maimed
maimed.text: Unconscious d6 rounds, then awaken with d4 HP. Infected, and a random body part destroyed.

stirs.name: Unconscious
stirs.text: Unconscious d4 rounds, then awaken with d4 HP.

narrowEscape.name: Narrow escape
narrowEscape.text: You narrowly avoid death. Alive and at 1 HP.

DeathsDoor.DrFrom: Sanity DR{dr}: 10, plus {count} for feats gained through Improving.
DeathsDoor.TestPurpose: Death's Door: on a Success you are unconscious for d8 rounds and wake with 1 HP. On a Failure you become a Dark Vessel.
DeathsDoor.Sleeps: {name} resists the pull of the dark.
DeathsDoor.Unconscious: Unconscious for {rounds}, then wakes with {hp} HP.
DeathsDoor.CountsInCombat: The rounds count down at the end of {name}'s own turns.
DeathsDoor.WakeByHand: Not in combat: the Dark Master presses Wake on the sheet when the time has passed.
DeathsDoor.Healed: {name} gains HP ({hp} HP now), wakes and is no longer at Death's Door.
DeathsDoor.BodyPart: Body part destroyed (d10: {roll}): {part}. Shown in Conditions.
DeathsDoor.LostText: Destroyed at Death's Door. The Dark Master decides what the loss does.
DeathsDoor.BecomesVessel: Something from beyond the light takes over {name}'s body: Dark Vessel with {hp} HP. Dark Vessels since the last Long Rest: {count}.
DeathsDoor.SecondVessel: A second Dark Vessel before a Long Rest. The body rises as a Shade, a foe under the Dark Master's control, and the player creates a new character.

Reason.killingBlow: Damage taken at Death's Door: {name} dies in a most gruesome manner.

DeathsDoor.StageRoll: At Death's Door: roll on the table.
DeathsDoor.StageTest: At Death's Door: test Sanity DR{dr} (button on the chat card).
DeathsDoor.StageWaking: Unconscious: {rounds} left, then wakes with {hp} HP.
DeathsDoor.WakeHint: Wake the character now with the HP the table gave. Use this outside combat when the rounds have passed.
DeathsDoor.VesselCount: Dark Vessels since a Long Rest
DeathsDoor.VesselHint: A second Dark Vessel before a Long Rest kills. Until resting exists, the Dark Master sets this back to 0 after a Long Rest.

Class.HpHint: Starting HP is this number plus Toughness, counted after the boost. It is fixed at creation.
Class.StartingDieHint: The die rolled on the armour and weaponry tables in 2.6 Starting Equipment.
Class.StartingWeaponsHint: Leave empty to roll on the weaponry table. Weapons chosen here are given instead, and the starting die is rolled on the armour table only (such as the Witch Hunter).

Background.WealthHint: As the rules write it, such as 2d6 × 10 s. Rolled and added to silver when the background is dropped on a character.
Background.KeepsakeHint: Added to the character's gear when the background is dropped on a character.

Origin.Heading: Origins
Origin.DropHint: Drag a class, an ancestry and a background onto this sheet. A new one replaces the old one.

Hint.class: Drop on a character: the boosted ability goes up 1, HP becomes this number + Toughness and max wounds are set.
Hint.ancestry: Drop on a character to record their ancestry. Add the chosen ancestry feat as a feat.
Hint.background: Drop on a character: wealth is rolled and added to silver, and the keepsake is added to their gear.

Origin.ReplaceBody: {actor} is already a {old}. Changing to {name} removes the class feature and every class power on the sheet, including powers gained by Improving, and gives the {name}'s starting feature and power. Hit Points and Wounds are set again for the new class.
Origin.BoostCapped: {ability} is already +6 and cannot go higher.
Origin.StartingDie: Roll a {die} on the armour and weaponry tables (2.6 Starting Equipment).
Origin.StartingDieFixed: Roll a {die} on the armour table only, and begin with: {weapons} (2.6 Starting Equipment).
Origin.Wealth: Wealth: {silver} s added. Silver is now {total} s.
Origin.NoWealth: No wealth rolled: the wealth is not written as dice, such as 2d6 × 10 s.

Outcome.failure: Half damage (rounded down), no other effect.

Power.NotYourTurn: {name} uses actions, so in combat it can only be used on your own turn.
Power.NotEnoughEmber: {name} costs 🟒{cost}, but the Ember pool holds only {left}.
Power.NoActions: Not enough actions left this turn; the pips are spent anyway.
Power.OutsideCombat: Outside combat: no Ember is spent. Each ember ability works once, until you finish an encounter or a rest.
Power.SustainNote: Sustained: press Sustain on the sheet on each of your turns, or it ends.
Power.NoClass: {name} has no class, so there is no key ability for this power.
Power.NoTarget: No target. Target a token to deal damage to it.
Power.UseNote: Costs 🟒{cost} from the Ember pool and {actions} action(s).
Power.SustainNotYourTurn: Sustain is an action, so in combat it can only be used on your own turn.
Power.AlreadyKept: {name} is already kept going until your next turn.
Power.NotSustained: {power} ends: {name} did not sustain it this turn.
Power.CostHint: The listed cost. The DR is always 11 + this, even if less is paid.
Power.ActionsHint: Actions it takes: ◈◈ is 2. 0 is a free action.
Power.DamageTypeHint: The kind of harm it deals: slashing, piercing or bludgeoning for blows, or the energy or other type the text names (fire, cold, light, mental…). Resistances, immunities and feats such as Firebug and Ancestral Resonance use it. None for no damage.
Power.DamageHint: The power's own damage dice, such as d6. Leave empty if it deals none.
Power.MagicHint: Autodidactism: tick if this power is magic-themed. A d6 is rolled after it: on a 1, a Photonic Surge.
Power.SustainedHint: Lasts while its user spends the Sustain action (◈) on each of their turns.
Power.ReactionHint: Used when its trigger happens, on anyone's turn. In combat it uses your reaction instead of actions.
Power.NoReaction: No reaction left this turn; it is used anyway. The Dark Master decides.
Power.UseNoteReaction: Costs 🟒{cost} from the Ember pool and your reaction (↻).
Power.OutcomesHint: Only fill these in if the power says something different. Empty uses the usual text.
Power.DrHint: Tests the class's boosted ability against DR{dr}.
Power.SustainTooltip: Keep this power going until your next turn (one action in combat).
Power.TestNote: Tests {ability} against DR{dr}: DR 11 + ember cost.
Power.AbilityHint: Leave on Usual for the class's boosted ability. Pick an ability only when the power names its own test (“Test Agility (DR18)”).
Power.DrHintNamed: Tests {ability}, as the power names, against DR{dr}.
Power.AddsWeaponHint: Tick for powers such as Power strike (“an additional d6”): the damage is a chosen weapon's damage dice plus the power's own, or unarmed (d2) or an improvised weapon (d4) without one. Only the dice: the weapon's traits do not apply, and it is not an attack.
Power.WeaponHint: Adds this weapon's damage dice to the power's. Its traits do not apply. Without a weapon: unarmed (d2) or an improvised weapon (d4).
Power.AlreadyUsed: {name} has already been used outside combat. It can be used again after an encounter or a rest, or when the Dark Master resets ember abilities.
Power.UsedOutsideHint: Used once outside combat. It works again after an encounter or a rest, or when the Dark Master resets ember abilities. In combat, pay from the Ember pool as usual.
Power.ResetTooltip: Every character's ember abilities can be used once again outside combat.
Power.ResetDone: Ember abilities are reset: each can be used once again outside combat.
Power.ResourceHint: Ember for a character's power, Gloom for a foe's gloom ability.
Power.GloomOnCharacter: {name} is a gloom ability. Gloom abilities belong to foes and are used from the foe sheet.
Power.NotEnoughEmberShort: Not enough Ember in the pool for {name}.

Spell.SheetHint: A spell, cast with Sanity against DR 11 + its ember cost (rules 3.11).
Spell.SpellListHint: Casting a spell outside your class's spell list is at Bane.
Spell.DamageHint: The spell's damage dice, such as d8. Leave empty if it deals none.
Spell.RitualHint: A ritual is cast over minutes or hours, outside combat, with no ember and no actions, at the DR of its tier (rules 4.7).
Spell.RitualDrHint: The DR of the ritual's tier heading: 14, 16, 18 or 20.
Spell.RitualTimeHint: How long the ritual takes, as the rules write it, such as 10 minutes.
Spell.RitualSheetDrHint: A ritual: Sanity against DR{dr}, outside combat, with no ember and no actions.
Spell.RitualInCombat: {name} is a ritual: it can only be cast outside combat.
Spell.RitualUseNote: A ritual ({time}): no ember and no actions.
Spell.RitualTestNote: Tests Sanity against DR{dr}: the DR of the ritual's tier. Its long casting time is already part of it, so there is no casting time choice.
Spell.OutcomesHint: Only fill these in if the spell says something different. Empty uses the usual text. A Ruin always calls for the Shadowblight table.

Outcome.failure: Half damage (rounded down), no other effect.
Outcome.ruin: No effect. Roll on the Shadowblight table.

Spell.TestNote: Tests Sanity against DR{dr}: DR 11 + ember cost.
Spell.OutsideListHint: This spell is on the {list} list; your class's list is {classList}. Untick it for a feature that removes the Bane, such as a spell in the Wizard's spellbook.
Spell.OutsideListChoose: This is a {list} spell. Your class chooses its spell list, so tick this if it is not the one you chose.
Spell.MetalArmourWorn: You wear {name}: metal armour of tier 2 or heavier smothers magic. Untick it only for a feature that removes the Bane.
Spell.MetalArmourHint: Metal armour of tier 2 or heavier gives Bane. Weapons and non-metal armour do not.
Spell.DuressHint: Tick if you cast under duress, such as with a foe within melee range.
Spell.SeveralCastersHint: Tick if more than one caster casts this spell, each spending the actions and ember in the same round.
Spell.ScrollSheetHint: A spell written on a scroll. Anyone can read it once, without Ember, testing Sanity against the spell's normal DR. It is destroyed when read, even if the spell fails (rules 3.11).
Spell.ScrollDrHint: Read from the scroll: Sanity against DR{dr}, no Ember.
Spell.ScrollTestNote: A scroll: tests Sanity against the spell's normal DR{dr}. No Ember, and no Bane for another spell list. The scroll is destroyed even if the spell fails.
Spell.ScrollNotYourTurn: You can only read {name} on your own turn.
Spell.ScrollNoEmber: Read from a scroll: no Ember spent.
Spell.ScrollSustainNote: A Sustained spell from a scroll: the scroll is gone, so keep track of sustaining it yourself (◈ each turn).
Spell.LifeForceHint: Test Toughness instead of Sanity, and lower the DR by {die} for each wound (never below DR6). Each wound tests Toughness as a wound at 0 HP, but HP does not change. You can spend up to {left}.
Spell.LifeForceNone: You are at your maximum wounds, so you cannot spend life force.
Spell.LifeForceNote: Life force: {count} wound(s), Toughness instead of Sanity, DR −{reduction} ({formula}: {dice}).
Spell.LifeForceAtMax: {name} is now at maximum wounds: the next 0 HP is Death's Door.
Spell.InSpellbookHint: Tome keeper: a spell written in your spellbook is never cast with the off-list Bane. Untick it if the book is lost.

Gloom.NotGloom: set to Ember, so it cannot be used
Gloom.CostHint: Paid from the Gloom pool in combat. Abilities cost 3, 5, 7 or 9.
Gloom.TestHint2: Leave on Usual unless the ability names its own test (“tests Presence DR12”).
Gloom.DrHint: The DR of the ability's own test. Weak foes use 12, Moderate 12 to 13, Strong 13 to 14, Mighty 14 to 16.
Gloom.DamageHint: The ability's damage dice, such as d6: half on a Success, full on a Failure, double on a Ruin.
Gloom.FailureDamageHint: Damage on a Failure, such as d6. Leave empty if none.
Gloom.RuinDamageHint: Damage on a Ruin, such as 2d6. Leave empty if none.
Gloom.ConditionHint: A condition the result gives. Set how long it lasts below.
Gloom.OutcomesHint: Write what each result does when the ability says (“Deafened until the end of its next turn”). Empty uses the usual text.
Gloom.NotYourTurn: {name} uses actions, so in combat a foe can only use it on its own turn.
Gloom.NotEnough: {name} costs ☾{cost}, but the Gloom pool holds only {left}.
Gloom.OutsideCombat: Outside combat: no Gloom is spent.
Gloom.TestHint: Each character it reaches makes the test.
Gloom.Gone: That gloom ability no longer exists.
Gloom.DefenceHint: Defence is Agility DR12. Heavy and special armour (+2 DR), a raised shield, Encumbered and conditions are added for you. Prone does not count. Armour soaks the damage.
Gloom.OwnHint: Armour penalties, Encumbered and conditions are added for you. Armour soaks the damage.

Kind.startOfTurn: Until the start of its next turn
Kind.encounter: Until the end of the encounter
Kind.escapeStart: Escape roll at the start of its turns (DR)
Kind.escapeEnd: Escape roll at the end of its turns (DR)

Timer.KeptLonger: It already had it for longer, so the longer time stays.
Timer.Ended: {name} is no longer {condition}: its time is up.
Timer.Button: Set how long this condition lasts
Timer.DialogHint: In combat, rounds count down at the end of each of its own turns; the turn it was gained in does not count. “Until the end of its next turn” is 1 round. Every timed condition ends when combat ends, except “Until the next day begins”, which ends at the next new day. Outside combat the timer does not run.
Timer.RoundsHint: A number such as 1, or dice such as d4. Dice are rolled when it is set.
Timer.BadRounds: “{rounds}” is not a number of rounds. Use a number such as 1, or dice such as d4.
Timer.FieldHint: How long the condition lasts. “Until the end of its next turn” is 1 round.
Timer.EscapeAsk: {name} tries to break free of {condition}: test Strength DR{dr}.
Timer.EscapeFree: {name} rolls {roll} (DR{dr}) and breaks free: no longer {condition}.

Shadowblight.NotYours: Only {name}'s owner or the Dark Master can roll on the Shadowblight table for them.
Shadowblight.Title: Shadowblight: {name}
Shadowblight.DmApplies: The Dark Master applies the result.
Shadowblight.Combustion: {name} knows {count} spell(s): the fireball reaches {feet} feet and deals {damage} damage.
Shadowblight.CombustionNone: {name} knows no spells: the fireball reaches 10 feet and deals no damage.

darknessEternal.name: Darkness eternal
darknessEternal.text: Light fades from your eyes; darkness engulfs your sight. You are Blinded for d10 days.

peerBeyondTheCurtain.name: Peer beyond the curtain
peerBeyondTheCurtain.text: The veil tears, your mind collapses through. There, a tattered page, your name scrawled in ink. You realise: you aren't real. This world is a hollow jest. A cruel farce. Roll on the Panic table with 2d10.

theWithering.name: The withering
theWithering.text: Your flesh begins to rot and peel. You are Doomed.

puppetry.name: Puppetry
puppetry.text: Your own shadow gains control of your body for d4 rounds, and you are forced to watch, immobile. It acts only in malice.

shatteredGround.name: Shattered ground
shatteredGround.text: The earth beneath your feet buckles, cracking open into jagged chasms. Everyone within 20 feet tests Agility DR14 or falls Prone, taking d4 damage.

mindRift.name: Mind rift
mindRift.text: Reality twists, your thoughts become foreign whispers, incomprehensible. Test Sanity DR16 or reduce your Sanity by 1 until you finish a rest.

bloodFog.name: Blood fog
bloodFog.text: A thick red mist surrounds you for 10 feet, lingering for 1d6 turns. All creatures within must test Toughness DR12 or suffer d4 persistent damage as they bleed profusely from every orifice.

corpseLight.name: Corpse-light
corpseLight.text: For 1d10 days, you emit an eerie, greenish glow that enrages any duskborn within a 1 mile radius. They're hostile to you specifically, are set on ending your life, and cannot be reasoned with.

hungerOfTheAbyss.name: Hunger of the abyss
hungerOfTheAbyss.text: A rift of pure darkness swallows you for 1d4 rounds. You are returned, but anything you carried on you is lost to the void.

echoesOfTheDead.name: Echoes of the dead
echoesOfTheDead.text: Voices from beyond tear into your mind, tormenting you. Lose 1 Fortune and take d4 persistent damage.

frozenBreath.name: Frozen breath
frozenBreath.text: Cold mist seeps from your skin, spreading a biting frost. For 1d6 hours, you are Slowed and all who touch you take d2 damage.

boneRot.name: Bone rot
boneRot.text: Your bones ache and weaken. Test Toughness DR12 after any form of physical impact; failure means you are Infected.

dustToDust.name: Dust to dust
dustToDust.text: Your flesh is not long for this world. You are Doomed. Every time you reduce your max HP, you age by the same amount.

theBirds.name: The birds
theBirds.text: Ravens and crows descend, pecking and clawing. Every creature within a 20-foot square takes d4 damage per round. The birds disperse after d6 rounds.

shatteredReflection.name: Shattered reflection
shatteredReflection.text: All reflective surfaces within 30 feet shatter into fragments, emitting an otherworldly screech that deals d4 damage to everyone within earshot.

fallingRocks.name: Falling rocks
fallingRocks.text: Boulders manifest right above you, crashing down upon you. Agility DR12 or gain a wound.

forgottenKnowledge.name: Forgotten knowledge
forgottenKnowledge.text: Something crucial is erased from your memory: perhaps a face, perhaps a ritual. Decide on one fact, memory, or spell; it is now completely lost to you.

darkbound.name: Darkbound
darkbound.text: Shadows permanently drag at your limbs. You cannot move when in darkness, and your movement is halved when in the light.

skinOfAsh.name: Skin of ash
skinOfAsh.text: Your skin becomes brittle and begins to flake away. You are Doomed, and suffer +2 DR to any social interactions until healed.

spontaneousCombustion.name: Spontaneous combustion
spontaneousCombustion.text: You explode in a massive fireball that reaches 10 feet, plus 5 feet for each spell you know. It deals 1d6 damage for each spell you know.

Calendar.Name: The Dusklands calendar
Calendar.Description: Ten months of 30 days, weeks of ten days. A new day begins at dawn.
Calendar.NextPhaseTooltip: Move the clock on to the next noon, dusk or dawn. At dawn the New day dialogue opens first.
Calendar.HourOnTooltip: Move the clock one hour on. Passing dawn opens the New day dialogue first.
Calendar.HourBackTooltip: Move the clock one hour back. It cannot go back before this day's dawn.
Calendar.NotBeforeDawn: The clock cannot go back before the dawn of the day that has begun: what the new day did cannot be undone.
Calendar.Waiting: The clock has passed dawn, but the new day has not begun. Press New day.
Calendar.DayWaiting: The clock has passed dawn. Press New day on the Calendar panel to begin the new day.
Calendar.Title: The Calendar
Calendar.Open: The Calendar: date, time of day, weather, Misery, New day and Rest

Weather.Label: Weather
Weather.Walled: Walled off at the edge of the flower: the weather stays {name}.
Weather.Shifts: On the road, the weather suddenly shifts.
Weather.Wrapped: Off the edge of the flower, it comes back in on the far side: {to}.
Weather.UntilNextDay: It lasts until the next day begins.
Weather.SetTooltip: Set today's weather by hand: pick a hex on the flower and, for a hazard, its event.
Weather.SetHint: Pick today's hex on the flower.
Weather.EventHint: Used only when the hex you pick is that hazard.
Weather.SetCard: The Dark Master sets the weather: {name}.

siltRain.Name: Silt rain
siltRain.Effect: A greasy, grey downpour coats everything in slick mud. Outdoors, all terrain is difficult terrain, and tracks wash away (tests to track are at Bane).

whistling.Name: Whistling from the Spine
whistling.Effect: An eerie whistling resounds across the realm, unnerving kin and kith. Bane on Panic tests, but the noise covers footsteps: Boon on tests to sneak outdoors.

creepfrost.Name: Creepfrost
creepfrost.Effect: A thin blue ice grows only on metal. Attacks with a metal weapon are at Bane unless its grip is wrapped in cloth or leather (an Interact action).

tamefire.Name: Tamefire
tamefire.Effect: Slow, wandering fires drift across the land without lasting harm to buildings. A creature that enters or starts its turn in a patch takes d4 persistent fire damage. The flames light the night: outdoors is never complete darkness today.

lightstrike.Name: Lightstrike
lightstrike.Effect: Thunder and lightning. At the start of each round of combat outdoors, roll a d6: 1 lightning strikes a random PC, 2 a random creature, 3–5 nothing, 6 a random foe. The target takes 2d6 damage. Creatures in metal armour of tier 2 or heavier are struck first.

hazefall.Name: Hazefall
hazefall.Effect: Runoff from the refineries settles as a metallic fog. No one can see more than 30'. Ranged attacks beyond 30' are at Bane, and a creature more than 30' away can hide without cover.

shadowstretch.Name: Shadowstretch
shadowstretch.Effect: Dim light stretches and sharpens every shadow. During an encounter, roll a d6 for each fresh corpse: on a 1, a Corpse Stealer takes hold of it and rises.

strongGales.Name: Strong gales
strongGales.Effect: Windy weather, stormy weather. Ranged attacks are at Bane, and creatures defend against ranged attacks with Boon. Flying creatures move at half speed. Each hour, roll a d6 for every torch or open flame outdoors: on a 1, it blows out.

blightPollen.Name: Blight-pollen
blightPollen.Effect: Black spores drift from twisted trees. For each hour outdoors without cloth over mouth and nose, test Toughness DR12: Failure Infected. Ruin Infected, and d4 damage as you cough up black dust.

loomingDark.Name: Looming dark
loomingDark.Effect: The clouds dip low and swallow the light. There is no daylight today: outdoors, anywhere your lights do not reach is complete darkness. Light sources work as normal.

dayOfGloom.Auto: the gloom pool fills 5 higher at the start of each round.
dayOfGloom.Name: Day of gloom
dayOfGloom.Effect: A sword day, a red day. In every combat, the gloom pool gains an extra 5 at the start of each round.

energyVoid.Auto: every combatant starts each turn Slowed; travel speed is halved.
energyVoid.Name: Energy void
energyVoid.Effect: Lethargy hangs heavy in the air. In combat, every creature is Slowed at the start of each of its turns. Out of combat, the day's travel covers only half as much ground.

heavyGravity.Name: Heavy gravity
heavyGravity.Effect: The essence of the world fluctuates and weighs everything down. Fall damage is doubled, Move is reduced by 5', and tests to lift, climb, jump or swim are at Bane. Flying creatures cannot gain height.

photonStorm.Name: Photon storm
photonStorm.Effect: Magic is abundant. Boon on tests to cast spells and use powers. The sky shimmers too brightly for stealth: Bane on tests to hide outdoors.

blackburn.Auto: the light timer burns twice as fast and lit tokens shine to half range.
blackburn.Name: Blackburn
blackburn.Effect: The dark is strong today. Light sources burn twice as fast and shed light in half their radius. The dark hides friend and foe alike: Boon on tests to hide in darkness.

oilmist.Name: Oilmist
oilmist.Effect: A prismatic vapour, safe to breathe but catastrophically flammable. Any open flame (a torch, a campfire, a firearm, a fire pot, a fire spell or power) ignites it. Everything within 10' of the flame tests Agility DR14: Failure 3d6 and d4 persistent fire damage. Ruin 4d6 and d6 persistent fire damage. The blast burns the mist away within 30' for the rest of the day. Closed lanterns are safe.

shadowblightOutbreak.Name: Shadowblight outbreak
shadowblightOutbreak.Effect: Magic becomes unstable. Bane on tests to cast spells and use powers, and a power that Ruins also rolls on the Shadowblight table.

lightGravity.Name: Light gravity
lightGravity.Effect: The essence of the world fluctuates and lets go. Fall damage is halved, jumps go twice as far, and tests to lift, climb, jump or swim are at Boon.

energyFont.Auto: every combatant starts each turn Quickened; travel speed is one and a half times.
energyFont.Name: Energy font
energyFont.Effect: Unnatural vitality invigorates everyone. In combat, every creature is Quickened at the start of each of its turns. Out of combat, the day's travel covers half as much ground again.

dayOfEmber.Auto: the ember pool fills 5 higher at the start of each round.
dayOfEmber.Name: Day of ember
dayOfEmber.Effect: A glorious day. In every combat, the ember pool gains an extra 5 at the start of each round.

Misery.Label: Misery
Misery.Name: Misery {numeral}
Misery.OmenHint: Setting the Misery rolls no omen unless you choose Roll the d6.
Misery.SetTooltip: Set the Misery by hand: its number, its omen, the group's light die, and whether the sun rose today.
Misery.SetHint: When will the light falter? The group picks the light die; a 1 on it at dawn brings the next Misery.
Misery.SetCard: The Dark Master sets the Misery: {name}.
Misery.EndText: All is lost. Nothing remains. The game and your lives end here. Burn your character sheets.

Omen.I1: The clouds turn the colour of bone, and ash rains down leaving a mark.
Omen.I2: The eyes of infants glow like the moon, as they babble only in dreams.
Omen.I3: The rivers run backwards for a day, returning all that was lost to the sea.
Omen.I4: All flowers bloom in the night, petals black as night.
Omen.I5: Statues weep rust, corroding until nothing but brittle skeletons remain.
Omen.I6: The Vigilant Bell rings. Bells of churches answer in kind, a midday funeral dirge.
Omen.II1: Wolves with eyes like empty sockets prowl the night, their howls echoing like the screams of the damned.
Omen.II2: A shadow without a master passes through every village, leaving frost in its wake.
Omen.II3: A thousand mirrors shatter in unison, each piece showing a different face.
Omen.II4: The forests bleed sap the colour of blood as the leaves whisper forgotten names.
Omen.II5: Birds take flight in the shape of a great serpent, vanishing into what little remains of the sun.
Omen.II6: Children speak in tongues unknown, their eyes unblinking until dusk.
Omen.III1: The moon wears a veil of crimson as shadows walk where no light should fall.
Omen.III2: The mountains groan, and from their peaks will spill rivers of molten silver.
Omen.III3: Twisted roots of black iron burst from the ground, strangling trees and poisoning the soil.
Omen.III4: An hourglass appears in every home, the sands within moving of their own accord.
Omen.III5: The sky itself flickers like a dying candle, revealing glimpses of a black void beyond.
Omen.III6: The wind will carry the scent of burning honey, and those who smell it will weep tears of flame.
Omen.IV1: The sky splits like old parchment, the stars bleed through the cracks.
Omen.IV2: All written words fade, as if ink and memory are consumed.
Omen.IV3: In the deepest caverns, a voice will cry out, and the stone will tremble with fear.
Omen.IV4: The sun will flicker, like a candle on its last breath, before burning twice as bright.
Omen.IV5: The ground will shift, and from every crack will sprout flowers that sing hymns of sorrow.
Omen.IV6: Crops grow black and twisted, and every bite tastes like ashes.
Omen.V1: The stars fall, each one striking the earth with the force of a hammer’s blow.
Omen.V2: Shadows consume their masters, leaving only empty shells that wander aimlessly.
Omen.V3: The moon will scream, and all who hear will be deafened by its agony.
Omen.V4: Stars begin to shiver in the night sky, flickering as if afraid of the darkness creeping in.
Omen.V5: The skulls of the dead begin to smile, their teeth glowing faintly in the dark.
Omen.V6: A beast with seven heads shall appear on the horizon, and every head will speak a different doom.
Omen.VI1: The sky blackens, and no fire shall burn, no flame shall kindle.
Omen.VI2: The ground cracks open as IT awakens, revealing an abyss that stretches forever.
Omen.VI3: The wind will cease, as all sound is swallowed in a silence more profound than death.
Omen.VI4: The stars shall turn to dust, falling as grey snow upon a shadowed world.
Omen.VI5: Every young heart shall beat once more, then stop in unison. These empty vessels shall not remain empty for long.
Omen.VI6: The moon is swallowed by a great shadow, leaving only a faint, blood-red ring in the sky.

Travel.Tooltip: Travel overland: spend the rest of this phase on the road, then roll the encounter table.
Travel.Title: Overland travel
Travel.SpendsPhase: The party travels for the rest of the {phase} phase. At its end, the encounter table is rolled.
Travel.BoonHint: Travelling by night, or through the Hinterlands, is more dangerous: the encounter table is rolled with Boon.
Travel.Cancelled: The new day did not begin, so the party did not travel.
Travel.Spent: The {phase} phase is spent on the road (×{speed} speed).
Travel.WeatherOffReroll: The weather is not in use, so the encounter d20 ({rolls}) was rolled again.
Travel.WeatherSlower: Energy void: the day's travel covers only half as much ground.
Travel.WeatherFaster: Energy font: the day's travel covers half as much ground again.
Travel.WeatherSlowerCard: {hazard}: only half as much ground today (×{speed} instead of ×{usual}).
Travel.WeatherFasterCard: {hazard}: half as much ground again today (×{speed} instead of ×{usual}).
Travel.CombatTables: Roll the encounter type and the type of creature on the Combat Tables.
Travel.OmenNone: An omen of the dying light.
Travel.Misfit: This hardship suits other places best. In the Heartlands, roll again or pick the nearest fit.
Travel.EachPC: Unless the entry says otherwise, every PC tests separately.

weather.Name: The weather suddenly shifts
weather.Text: The weather moves on the hex flower using 2d6.

scenery.Name: Scenery
scenery.Text: The Dark Master describes something seen along the way.

blackout.Name: Blackout
blackout.Effect: The sky gutters like a dying wick and darkness engulfs the land for d4 hours. Without a light source, the party is in complete darkness (Bane on all tests) and rolls for a random encounter for every hour spent in it.

waylaid.Name: Waylaid
waylaid.Effect: The roads have shifted, or the landmarks have been swallowed. One PC tests Presence DR12 to find the way. Failure: the party loses d4 hours. Ruin: the party loses a whole phase and rolls on the encounter table again.

thinIce.Name: Thin Ice
thinIce.Effect: A frozen river or mire looks solid, but cracks beneath your weight. Test Agility DR12. Failure: you plunge into the freezing water before being pulled out: d4 damage and one level of Fatigued. Ruin: as Failure, and one carried item of the Dark Master's choice is lost beneath the ice.

coldSnap.Name: Cold Snap
coldSnap.Effect: A sudden drop in temperature catches even the hardened off guard; breath crystallises in the air. Test Toughness DR12 (Boon with cold weather clothes). Failure: d6 damage. Ruin: d6 damage and one level of Fatigued that is not removed until you rest somewhere warm.

howlingGale.Name: Howling Gale
howlingGale.Effect: Razor-sharp winds batter the travellers, numbing fingers and drowning out all sound. Unshielded torches and candles go out. Test Toughness DR12. Failure: one level of Fatigued. Ruin: one level of Fatigued, and Deafened until your next Long Rest.

rockslide.Name: Rockslide
rockslide.Effect: A distant rumble becomes a roaring wall of snow and stone. Test Agility DR14. Failure: 2d6 damage, and you are Restrained (buried) until an ally spends ◈◈ to dig you out. Ruin: 3d6 damage and Restrained (buried). Each round you stay buried, take d4 damage.

spoiledSupplies.Name: Spoiled Supplies
spoiledSupplies.Effect: Rations freeze, rot or turn to ash in their wrappings. Each PC rolls the expendable die of every food and water item they carry.

ashfall.Name: Ashfall
ashfall.Effect: The clouds turn the colour of bone, and grey ash drifts down like snow. Test Toughness DR12. Failure: d4 damage and a hacking cough: Bane on Presence tests until your next Long Rest. Ruin: as Failure, and you are Infected.

fallingLedge.Name: Falling Ledge
fallingLedge.Effect: An overhang of rotten stone and snow gives way beneath the party. Test Agility DR12. Failure: you slide and fall 10' (no damage) and land Prone. The party loses d4 hours regrouping. Ruin: you fall 20': 10 damage, and you land Prone.

dryLightning.Name: Dry Lightning
dryLightning.Effect: A storm without rain crackles across the plain, hunting the tallest point. The PC carrying the most metal tests Agility DR12. Failure: 2d6 damage. Ruin: 3d6 damage, and your armour is reduced by one tier.

frostbite.Name: Frostbite
frostbite.Effect: Hours of biting wind leave flesh pale and numb. Test Toughness DR12 (Boon with cold weather clothes). Failure: Bane on Agility tests until you rest somewhere warm. Ruin: you gain a wound as fingers or toes blacken and die.

bitterClimb.Name: Bitter Climb
bitterClimb.Effect: A sheer, wind-scoured ascent or a road sunk into mud saps the strength from your limbs. Test Strength DR12. Failure: one level of Fatigued. Ruin: one level of Fatigued and d4 damage, and you drop one carried item of your choice down the slope.

whistlingWinds.Name: Whistling Winds
whistlingWinds.Effect: You now know why it is called the Whistling Spine: the wind howls through the old quarries and carries whispers that burrow into the mind. Test Sanity DR12. Failure: you are Stupefied until the end of your next encounter. Ruin: test for Panic. Until your next Long Rest, you are deeply suspicious of strangers.

watcher.Name: The Watcher on the Ridge
watcher.Effect: Through the haze, a pale figure stands motionless on a distant ridge, its eyes gleaming like cold moons. For a moment, you cannot look away. Test Sanity DR14. Failure: you are Frightened of the figure until your next Long Rest, and certain it is following you. Ruin: roll on the Panic table with d10. Your next Long Rest gives no benefit, as you wake again and again to check the dark.

mournfulDirge.Name: Mournful Dirge
mournfulDirge.Effect: The wind carries a funeral bell from somewhere far away, mournful and sweet: Harkin calling someone home. Test Sanity DR12. Failure: your next Long Rest gives no benefit; the bell tolls in your dreams. Ruin: as Failure, and you have Bane on Panic tests until that rest is complete.

oilmist.Name: Oilmist
oilmist.Effect: A shimmering, oily haze settles over the land for d4 hours. It is safe to breathe but catastrophically flammable. Any open flame in it explodes: everyone within 20' tests Agility DR14. Failure: 3d6 damage and d4 persistent fire damage. Ruin: 4d6 damage and d6 persistent fire damage. Lanterns with a closed shutter are safe.

foulAir.Name: Foul Air
foulAir.Effect: The party wanders into a pocket of gas seeping from the deep strata. Test Toughness DR12. Failure: d6 damage and one level of Fatigued. Ruin: d6 damage and d4 persistent poison damage.

moondrops.Name: Moondrops
moondrops.Effect: An untouched clearing of ice-crystal flowers pulses faintly with inner light. As you linger, the air grows still and a gentle warmth fills your chest. Until your next Long Rest, you ignore the effects of non-magical cold, including results 3, 4 and 11 on this table.

silverEye.Name: The Silver Eye
silverEye.Effect: The clouds part to reveal the cold, pure light of the moon, and for a fleeting moment something passes judgement. Each PC rolls the Chance Die. Positive: regain 1 Fortune. Neutral: nothing happens. Negative: Bane on your next test.

wayshrine.Name: Wayshrine
wayshrine.Effect: A roadside cairn, its lamp still burning, shelters a shrine to a half-forgotten god. The party may take a Long Rest here without testing for interruptions, and anyone who leaves an offering of food or light regains d4 HP.

Minion.Made: {item}: {name} is now {owner}’s {tier}. Pick its abilities with the Dark Master and write them on its sheet.
Minion.AskDm: {item}: making a minion needs the right to create actors. Ask the Dark Master to press the Use button.

TierAbilities.moderate: one passive and one ◈◈ active ability

Minion.TierHint: This tier: HP {hp}, Morale {morale}, armour {armour}, attack {attack}, {abilities} (rules 3.14).
Minion.ApplyTierAsk: Set HP, Morale, armour and the first attack's damage to those of a {tier}? What is there now is replaced.
Minion.OwnerHint: The character it serves. A character can have minions up to their Presence (minimum 1); an owner already at the limit is refused. The owner's players can command it and roll for it.
Minion.RulesHint: A minion has 2 actions and 0 reactions, and acts only when commanded (◈). It tests, attacks and defends at +0, has no Fortune and no wounds, and dies at 0 HP. In combat it acts right after its owner.
Minion.MoraleHint: Roll 2d6: above its Morale, the minion is demoralised. Morale – never rolls.
Minion.ArmourHint: Subtracted from damage that hits the minion. A defence Ruin steps it down one.
Minion.AttackTooltip: Attack at +0: opens the attack dialogue
Minion.DropHint: Drag weapons (attacks) and feats (passives and active abilities) from the Items sidebar onto this sheet, or use the Add buttons.
Minion.Heading: Minions ({count}/{limit})
Minion.LimitHint: You can have minions up to your Presence (minimum 1). Every minion counts, summoned ones too (rules 3.14).
Minion.NoneYet: None. Give a minion this character as its owner on the minion's sheet.
Minion.CommandTooltip: Command a minion (◈): in combat, on your own turn, spend one action. Its turn, right after yours, has two actions.
Minion.OverLimit: {owner} already has {limit} minions, their limit (Presence, minimum 1). Dismiss, release or abandon one before {name} can join.
Minion.NotYourTurn: You can only command a minion on your own turn.
Minion.NotInCombat: {name} is not in this combat. Add its token to the Combat Tracker first.
Minion.NotYours: You do not own {name}. Ask the Dark Master to give it an owner on its sheet.
Minion.AlreadyCommanded: {name} has already been commanded for its next turn.
Minion.NoActions: No actions left this turn. The command is given anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Minion.Commanded: {owner} commands {name} (◈). It acts right after {owner}, with two actions.
Minion.TurnIdle: {name} was not commanded by {owner}: no actions. It only acts to escape obvious harm.
Minion.Fell: {name} falls at 0 HP and is dead.

Relic.SheetHint: The Description box below is the relic's effect. Every relic has the Expendable d20 trait: after each use roll a d20, and on a 1 it is used up (rules 4.2).
Relic.AlwaysOnHint: Its effect is always on, like the rebreather or the compass. Instead of Use it has a Daily roll: the Expendable d20, once per day, the first time its effect matters.
Relic.EmberGainHint: Added to the Ember pool when the relic is used, such as 3 for the Shard of the Great Brazier. Only in combat, as there is no pool outside it. Leave at 0 for none.
Relic.DestroyedHint: Used up or burnt out by its Last Rite: its drawback applies. Untick it when the relic is recovered; it can then be used again.
Relic.DestroyedTooltip: Destroyed. Untick Destroyed on the relic if it is recovered.
Relic.SaleValueHint: What a fence or collector pays. Its drawback strikes the moment it leaves your hands.
Relic.FactionValueHint: What its faction pays to take it home. Then the drawback does not apply.
Relic.DrawbackHint: This relic is destroyed, so its drawback applies until it is recovered.
Relic.UseTooltip: Use it: posts its effect, then rolls the Expendable d20
Relic.DailyTooltip: Daily roll: the Expendable d20, the first time today its effect matters
Relic.LastRiteTooltip: Last Rite: it always works, needs no ember and no Expendable roll, and destroys the relic
Relic.UsedUp: Used up: the relic is destroyed!
Relic.IsDestroyed: {item} is destroyed. Untick Destroyed on it if it is recovered.
Relic.NeedsCombat: {item} adds to the Ember pool, and there is no pool outside combat.
Relic.LastRiteAsk: Burn {item} out for its Last Rite? It always works, and the relic is destroyed.
Relic.LastRiteRule: A Last Rite always works, needs no ember and no Expendable roll.
Relic.BurntOut: The relic is burnt out and destroyed.
Relic.RecoverHint: If it is recovered, the Dark Master unticks Destroyed on the relic.

Chest.ContentsHint: What is inside. Drag an item onto your character sheet to take it, or from your sheet onto this list to put it in.
Chest.DragHint: Drag items out to take them, or in to leave them here.
Chest.NoToken: You need a token on this scene to open {name}.
Chest.TooFar: Stand next to {name} to open it.
Chest.CannotHold: {item} cannot be put in a chest.
Chest.NeedGM: The Dark Master must be logged in to move items in or out of a chest.
Chest.OnlyGMAdds: Only the Dark Master can put new items in a chest. Drag one from your character sheet instead.
Chest.NoSilverTaker: Stand next to {name} with your token to take the silver.
Chest.SplitHint: Share the silver equally among the characters of the players logged in now (each player's character is set in User Configuration). What cannot be split stays in the chest.
Chest.SplitLeft: {left} s could not be split and stays in the chest.
